Write function to round 0.5 up and not down.

```{r}
#| warning: false

# function to round correctly

round2 = function(x, digits) {
  posneg = sign(x)
  z = abs(x)*10^digits
  z = z + 0.5 + sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
  z = trunc(z)
  z = z/10^digits
  z*posneg
}

```

```{r}
unibePalettes <- function(plot = TRUE){
  x <- palette <- NULL

  cols <- c("unibeRedS", "unibeBlackS", "unibeIceS", "unibeSaphireS", "unibeOceanS",
    "unibeVioletS", "unibeBrownS", "unibeMintS", "unibePastelS", "unibeIceS",
    "unibeMustardS", "unibeApricotS")

  dat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cols,
    function(name){
      fn <- get(name)
      # print(name)
      values <- fn()
      data.frame(palette = name,
                 x = 1:length(values),
                 cols = values)
    }))

  dat$palette <- factor(dat$palette, cols)

  if(plot){

    pals <- dat
    pals$x2 <- pals$x + 1
    pals$y <- as.numeric(factor(pals$palette, rev(unique(pals$palette)))) - .5
    pals$y2 <- as.numeric(factor(pals$palette, rev(unique(pals$palette)))) + .5

    oldpar <- par(mai = c(.5, 1.5, .5, .5))
    on.exit(par(oldpar))

    plot(1,1,type = "n",
         xlim = c(min(pals$x, pals$x2), max(pals$x, pals$x2)),
         ylim = c(min(pals$y, pals$y2), max(pals$y, pals$y2)),
         xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", bty = "n")
    with(pals, rect(x, y, x2, y2, col = cols, border = NA))
    axis(at = as.numeric(unique(factor(pals$palette, rev(unique(pals$palette))))),
         labels = unique(factor(pals$palette, rev(unique(pals$palette)))),
         side = 2, las = 2)
    axis(side = 1, at = unique(pals$x) + .5, labels = unique(pals$x))

  } else {
    dat
  }

}


unibeScales <- function() c("unibeRedS", "unibeBlackS", "unibeIceS", "unibeSaphireS", "unibeOceanS",
                            "unibeVioletS", "unibeBrownS", "unibeMintS", "unibePastelS", "unibeIceS",
                            "unibeMustardS", "unibeApricotS")

```

## Coding variables

### Age group


```{r}


data_height_clean <- data_height_clean |> 
  mutate(age_group_height = case_when(age_years_height < 1 ~ "Infancy: <1",
                               age_years_height < 6 ~ "Preschool age: 1–5",
                               age_years_height < 12 ~ "School age: 6–11",
                               age_years_height >= 12 ~ "Adolescence: 12–17")) |> 
  mutate(age_group_height = factor(age_group_height, levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17")))


data_weight_clean <- data_weight_clean |> 
  mutate(age_group_weight = case_when(age_years_weight < 1 ~ "Infancy: <1",
                               age_years_weight < 6 ~ "Preschool age: 1–5",
                               age_years_weight < 12 ~ "School age: 6–11",
                               age_years_weight >= 12 ~ "Adolescence: 12–17")) |> 
  mutate(age_group_weight = factor(age_group_weight, levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17")))


data_head <- data_head |> 
  mutate(age_group_head = case_when(age_years_circumference < 1 ~ "Infancy: <1",
                               age_years_circumference < 6 ~ "Preschool age: 1–5",
                               age_years_circumference < 12 ~ "School age: 6–11",
                               age_years_circumference >= 12 ~ "Adolescence: 12–17")) |> 
  mutate(age_group_head = factor(age_group_head, levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17")))



data_bmi <- data_bmi |> 
  mutate(age_group_bmi = case_when(age_years_bmi < 1 ~ "Infancy: <1",
                                   age_years_bmi < 6 ~ "Preschool age: 1–5",
                               age_years_bmi < 12 ~ "School age: 6–11",
                               age_years_bmi >= 12 ~ "Adolescence: 12–17")) |> 
  mutate(age_group_bmi = factor(age_group_bmi, levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17")))


```

I use tables of interpolated LMS-values to calculate z-scores of height, weight and BMI.

I define a function to calculate z-scores. I use the correction method of the WHO for z-scores <-3 and >+3, see [here](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/child-growth/growth-reference-5-19-years/computation.pdf).

```{r}
#| output: false
#| warning: false

# function to calculate z-scores -----

z_score_calc = function(L,M,S,parameter){
  if(is.na(L)|is.na(M)|is.na(S)|is.na(parameter)|parameter <= 0){
    return(NA)
  }
  z_score = ((parameter/M)^L-1)/(S*L)
  return(z_score)
}

# function to calculate corrected z-scores as described by the WHO. -----

z_score_calc_corr = function(L,M,S,parameter){
  if(is.na(L)|is.na(M)|is.na(S)|is.na(parameter)|parameter <= 0){
    return(NA)
  }
  z_score = ((parameter/M)^L-1)/(S*L)
  if (z_score > 3){
    SD3pos = M*(1+S*L*3)^(1/L)
    SD2pos = M*(1+S*L*2)^(1/L)
    SD23pos = SD3pos - SD2pos
    z_score = 3+((parameter-SD3pos)/SD23pos)
    return(z_score)
  } else if (z_score < -3){
    SD3neg = M*(1+S*L*(-3))^(1/L)
    SD2neg = M*(1+S*L*(-2))^(1/L)
    SD23neg = SD2neg - SD3neg
    z_score = -3+((parameter-SD3neg)/SD23neg)
    return(z_score)
  } else{
    return(z_score)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| output: false

  left_join(y=interpolated_braegger_height_length, by = c('age_days_z' = "age_days",'sex'))

  ungroup()
```

## Inclusion criteria

Inclusion criteria of SwissPedGrowth (already applied)

Inclusion criteria for this analysis:
•	Children who had a plausible height, weight, BMI or head circumference measurement between 0 to 18 years.

Exclude:
•	AND excluded implausible height, weight, BMI or head circumference measurements.
•	AND excluded children with missing information on age or sex


```{r}
cat("Number participants in SwissPedGrowth\n")
data_participant |> nrow()

cat("Number of measurements in SwissPedGrowth\n")
data_height_clean |> nrow()
data_weight_clean |> nrow()
data_bmi |> nrow()
data_head |> nrow()


```


### Population 1: 'all children'

```{r}

data_height_clean <- data_height_clean |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(age_years_height) ~ "No age at height",
                                      (age_years_height >= 18) ~ "Height after 18",
                                      combined_result == "Missing - Recording" | combined_result == "Missing - Age" ~ "Invalid information",
                                      combined_result == "Exclude - Longitudinal-Outlier" | combined_result == "Exclude - Single-Outlier" | combined_result == "Exclude - Z-Score" ~ "Outlier",
                                      combined_result == "Carried-Forward" | combined_result == "Same-Day" ~ "Duplicate",
                                      is.na(sex) ~ "Missing sex",
                                      TRUE ~ "Include")) |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = factor(include_analysis_pop1,
                                   levels = c("Include", "No age at height", "Height after 18", "Duplicate", "Outlier", "Invalid information", "Missing sex")))

data_height_clean |> select(include_analysis_pop1) |>  tbl_summary()


data_weight_clean <- data_weight_clean |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(age_years_weight) ~ "No age at weight",
                                      (age_years_weight >= 18) ~ "weight after 18",
                                      combined_result == "Missing - Recording" | combined_result == "Missing - Age" ~ "Invalid information",
                                      combined_result == "Exclude - Longitudinal-Outlier" | combined_result == "Exclude - Single-Outlier" | combined_result == "Exclude - Z-Score" ~ "Outlier",
                                      combined_result == "Carried-Forward" | combined_result == "Same-Day" ~ "Duplicate",
                                      is.na(sex) ~ "Missing sex",
                                      TRUE ~ "Include")) |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = factor(include_analysis_pop1,
                                   levels = c("Include", "No age at weight", "weight after 18", "Duplicate", "Outlier", "Invalid information", "Missing sex")))

data_weight_clean |> select(include_analysis_pop1) |>  tbl_summary()

data_head <- data_head |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(age_days_circumference) ~ "No age at head",
                                      (age_years_circumference >= 18) ~ "Head after 18",
                                      manual_result == "Zero-or-negative-circumference" | manual_result == "Negative-age" ~ "Invalid information",
                                      manual_result == "Exclude - Z-Score" ~ "Outlier",
                                      manual_result == "Carried-Forward" | manual_result == "Same-Day" ~ "Duplicate",
                                      is.na(sex) ~ "Missing sex",
                                      TRUE ~ "Include")) |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = factor(include_analysis_pop1,
                                   levels = c("Include", "No age at head", "Head after 18", "Duplicate", "Outlier", "Invalid information", "Missing sex")))

data_head |> select(include_analysis_pop1) |>  tbl_summary()


data_bmi <- data_bmi |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(age_days_bmi) ~ "No age at bmi",
                                      (age_years_bmi >= 18) ~ "BMI after 18",
                                      combined_result_bmi == "Missing Weight - Recording" | combined_result_bmi == "Missing Weight - Age" ~ "Invalid information",
                                      combined_result_bmi == "Missing Height - Recording" | combined_result_bmi == "Missing Height - Age" ~ "Invalid information",
                                      combined_result_bmi == "Exclude Weight - Longitudinal-Outlier" | combined_result_bmi == "Exclude Weight - Single-Outlier" | combined_result_bmi == "Exclude Weight - Z-Score" ~ "Outlier",
                                      combined_result_bmi == "Exclude Height - Longitudinal-Outlier" | combined_result_bmi == "Exclude Height - Single-Outlier" | combined_result_bmi == "Exclude Height - Z-Score" ~ "Outlier",
                                      combined_result_bmi == "Exclude BMI - Z-Score" ~ "Outlier",
                                      combined_result_bmi == "Duplicate Weight - Carried-Forward" | combined_result_bmi == "Duplicate Weight - Same-Day" ~ "Duplicate",
                                      combined_result_bmi == "Duplicate Height - Carried-Forward" | combined_result_bmi == "Duplicate Height - Same-Day" ~ "Duplicate",
                                      is.na(sex) ~ "Missing sex",
                                      TRUE ~ "Include")) |> 
  mutate(include_analysis_pop1 = factor(include_analysis_pop1,
                                   levels = c("Include", "No age at bmi", "BMI after 18", "Duplicate", "Outlier", "Invalid information", "Missing sex")))

data_bmi |> select(include_analysis_pop1) |>  tbl_summary()

```


```{r}

data_participant <- data_participant |> 
  left_join(data_height_clean |>
              filter(include_analysis_pop1 == "Include" | include_analysis_pop1 == "Missing sex") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_height_measurements" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |>
  left_join(data_weight_clean |>
              filter(include_analysis_pop1 == "Include" | include_analysis_pop1 == "Missing sex") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_weight_measurements" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |> 
  left_join(data_bmi |>
              filter(include_analysis_pop1 == "Include" | include_analysis_pop1 == "Missing sex") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_bmi_measurements" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |> 
  left_join(data_head |>
              filter(include_analysis_pop1 == "Include" | include_analysis_pop1 == "Missing sex") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_head_measurements" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id")

data_participant <- data_participant |> 
  mutate(include_height_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(number_height_measurements) ~ "Exclude - no height",
                                                  is.na(sex) ~ "Exclude - no sex",
                                                  is.na(birth_date) ~ "Exclude - no birth date",
                                                  TRUE ~ "Include"),
         include_weight_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(number_weight_measurements) ~ "Exclude - no weight",
                                                  is.na(sex) ~ "Exclude - no sex",
                                                  is.na(birth_date) ~ "Exclude - no birth date",
                                                  TRUE ~ "Include"),
         include_bmi_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(number_bmi_measurements) ~ "Exclude - no bmi",
                                                  is.na(sex) ~ "Exclude - no sex",
                                                  is.na(birth_date) ~ "Exclude - no birth date",
                                                  TRUE ~ "Include"),
         include_head_analysis_pop1 = case_when(is.na(number_head_measurements) ~ "Exclude - no head",
                                                  is.na(sex) ~ "Exclude - no sex",
                                                  is.na(birth_date) ~ "Exclude - no birth date",
                                                  TRUE ~ "Include")) |> 
  select(-c(number_height_measurements, number_weight_measurements, number_bmi_measurements, number_head_measurements))

data_participant |> 
  select(include_height_analysis_pop1, include_weight_analysis_pop1, include_bmi_analysis_pop1, include_head_analysis_pop1) |> 
  tbl_summary()


```

### Apply inclusion criteria


```{r}

data_participant_height_pop1 <- data_participant_height_pop1 |> 
  left_join(data_height_pop1 |>
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_height_measurements_total" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |> 
  mutate(height_measurement_total = case_when(number_height_measurements_total == 1 ~ "One",
                                           number_height_measurements_total == 2 ~ "Two",
                                           number_height_measurements_total >2 ~ "Three or more")) |> 
  left_join(data_height_pop1 |>
              filter(age_group_height == "Infancy: <1") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_height_measurements_infancy" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |> 
  mutate(height_measurement_infancy = case_when(number_height_measurements_infancy >= 1 ~ "yes",
                                        is.na(number_height_measurements_infancy) ~ "no")) |> 
  left_join(data_height_pop1 |>
              filter(age_group_height == "Preschool age: 1–5") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_height_measurements_preschool" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |> 
  mutate(height_measurement_preschool = case_when(number_height_measurements_preschool >= 1 ~ "yes",
                                        is.na(number_height_measurements_preschool) ~ "no")) |> 
  left_join(data_height_pop1 |>
              filter(age_group_height == "School age: 6–11") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_height_measurements_school" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |> 
  mutate(height_measurement_school = case_when(number_height_measurements_school >= 1 ~ "yes",
                                        is.na(number_height_measurements_school) ~ "no")) |> 
  left_join(data_height_pop1 |>
              filter(age_group_height == "Adolescence: 12–17") |> 
              count(participant_id) |> rename("number_height_measurements_adolescence" = "n"),
            by = "participant_id") |> 
  mutate(height_measurement_adolescence = case_when(number_height_measurements_adolescence >= 1 ~ "yes",
                                        is.na(number_height_measurements_adolescence) ~ "no"))


data_height_pop1 <- data_height_pop1 |>
```

# Analysis weights

## Population 1 analysis: all children


Every participant should contribute the same amount to the analysis, whether they had 1 or 5 measurements.

```{r}

data_height_pop1 <- data_height_pop1 |>  
  mutate(analysis_weight = 1/number_height_measurements_total)

data_weight_pop1 <- data_weight_pop1 |> 
  mutate(analysis_weight = 1/number_weight_measurements_total)

data_head_pop1 <- data_head_pop1 |> 
  mutate(analysis_weight = 1/number_head_measurements_total)

data_bmi_pop1 <- data_bmi_pop1 |> 
  mutate(analysis_weight = 1/number_bmi_measurements_total)

```


## Population 2 analysis: Normal growth & weighted

### eFigure: Weighting love plot

#### Height

Summary statistics before weighting

```{r}

data_height_pop2 <- data_height_pop2 |>
  mutate(analysis_weight = 1/number_height_measurements_total)

```


```{r}

data_participant_height_pop2 |> 
  select(sex, height_measurement_infancy, height_measurement_preschool, height_measurement_school, height_measurement_adolescence, nationality_group_middle, swiss_sep_3, swiss_sep_3_quintile, hospital, number_height_measurements_total) |> 
  tbl_summary(type = list(all_continuous() ~ "continuous2",
                             all_dichotomous() ~ "categorical"),
              statistic = list(all_continuous2() ~ c("{mean} ({sd})", "{median} ({p25}, {p75})", "{min}, {max}"),
                               all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"),
              missing = "ifany",
```

Weighting using raking and survey package


```{r}

# target margins of the genpop

pop.age <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "Age") |> 
  mutate(age = factor(Group,
                      levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(age, Freq)
  
pop.sex <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "Sex") |> 
  mutate(sex = factor(Group,
                      levels = c("Female", "Male"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(sex, Freq)

pop.nationality <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "Nationality") |> 
  filter(Group != "Missing") |> 
  mutate(nationality = factor(Group,
                      levels = c("Swiss", "Northern/Western Europe", "Southern/Eastern Europe", "Other"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(nationality, Freq)


pop.ssep <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "SSEP") |> 
  mutate(swiss_sep_3_quintile = factor(Group,
                                     levels = c("Quintile 1", "Quintile 2","Quintile 3","Quintile 4","Quintile 5"),
                                     labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(swiss_sep_3_quintile, Freq)


data_to_rake_height_pop2 <- data_height_pop2 |>
  select(height_id, participant_id, age_group_height, sex, nationality_group_middle, swiss_sep_3_quintile, analysis_weight) |> 
  mutate(age = factor(age_group_height,
                      levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17"),
                      labels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17")),
         sex = factor(case_when(sex == "f" ~ "Female",
                                sex == "m" ~ "Male"),
                      levels = c("Female", "Male")),
         nationality = factor(nationality_group_middle,
                              levels = c("Swiss", "Northern/Western Europe", "Southern/Eastern Europe", "Other")),
         swiss_sep_3_quintile = factor(swiss_sep_3_quintile,
                                     levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))) |> 
  select(height_id, participant_id, age, sex, nationality, swiss_sep_3_quintile, analysis_weight) |> 
  drop_na()



data_raked_height_pop2 <- rake(svydesign(ids = ~participant_id, data = data_to_rake_height_pop2, weights = ~analysis_weight),
                        sample.margins = list(~age, ~sex, ~nationality, ~swiss_sep_3_quintile),
                        population.margins = list(pop.age, pop.sex, pop.nationality, pop.ssep))

weights_height_pop2 <- data.frame(height_id = data_to_rake_height_pop2$height_id,
                                      genpop_weight = weights(data_raked_height_pop2),
                                      stabilized_genpop_weight = weights(data_raked_height_pop2)/mean(weights(data_raked_height_pop2)))

summary(weights_height_pop2$stabilized_genpop_weight)


# add weights back to data

data_height_pop2 <- data_height_pop2 |> 
  left_join(weights_height_pop2 |> select(height_id, genpop_weight), by = "height_id")

data_height_pop2 <- data_height_pop2 |> 
  mutate(genpop_analysis_weight = genpop_weight/number_height_measurements_total,
         stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight = genpop_analysis_weight*39486/sum(genpop_analysis_weight))

sum(data_height_pop2$genpop_weight)
sum(data_height_pop2$genpop_analysis_weight)
sum(data_height_pop2$stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

summary(data_height_pop2$stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

rm(data_to_rake_height_pop2, data_raked_height_pop2)
```

Weighting using raking and survey package


```{r}

# target margins of the genpop

pop.age <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "Age") |> 
  mutate(age = factor(Group,
                      levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(age, Freq)
  
pop.sex <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "Sex") |> 
  mutate(sex = factor(Group,
                      levels = c("Female", "Male"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(sex, Freq)

pop.nationality <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "Nationality") |> 
  filter(Group != "Missing") |> 
  mutate(nationality = factor(Group,
                      levels = c("Swiss", "Northern/Western Europe", "Southern/Eastern Europe", "Other"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(nationality, Freq)


pop.ssep <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "SSEP") |> 
  mutate(swiss_sep_3_quintile = factor(Group,
                                     levels = c("Quintile 1", "Quintile 2","Quintile 3","Quintile 4","Quintile 5"),
                                     labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(swiss_sep_3_quintile, Freq)


data_to_rake_head_pop2 <- data_head_pop2 |>
  select(circumference_id, participant_id, age_group_head, sex, nationality_group_middle, swiss_sep_3_quintile, analysis_weight) |> 
  mutate(age = factor(age_group_head,
                      levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17"),
                      labels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17")),
         sex = factor(case_when(sex == "f" ~ "Female",
                                sex == "m" ~ "Male"),
                      levels = c("Female", "Male")),
         nationality = factor(nationality_group_middle,
                              levels = c("Swiss", "Northern/Western Europe", "Southern/Eastern Europe", "Other")),
         swiss_sep_3_quintile = factor(swiss_sep_3_quintile,
                                     levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))) |> 
  select(circumference_id, participant_id, age, sex, nationality, swiss_sep_3_quintile, analysis_weight) |> 
  drop_na()



data_raked_head_pop2 <- rake(svydesign(ids = ~participant_id, data = data_to_rake_head_pop2, weights = ~analysis_weight),
                        sample.margins = list(~age, ~sex, ~nationality, ~swiss_sep_3_quintile),
                        population.margins = list(pop.age, pop.sex, pop.nationality, pop.ssep))

weights_head_pop2 <- data.frame(circumference_id = data_to_rake_head_pop2$circumference_id,
                                      genpop_weight = weights(data_raked_head_pop2),
                                      stabilized_genpop_weight = weights(data_raked_head_pop2)/mean(weights(data_raked_head_pop2)))

summary(weights_head_pop2$stabilized_genpop_weight)


# add weights back to data

data_head_pop2 <- data_head_pop2 |> 
  left_join(weights_head_pop2 |> select(circumference_id, genpop_weight), by = "circumference_id")

data_head_pop2 <- data_head_pop2 |> 
  mutate(genpop_analysis_weight = genpop_weight/number_head_measurements_total,
         stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight = genpop_analysis_weight*13007/sum(genpop_analysis_weight))

sum(data_head_pop2$genpop_weight)
sum(data_head_pop2$genpop_analysis_weight)
sum(data_head_pop2$stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

summary(data_head_pop2$stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

rm(data_to_rake_head_pop2, data_raked_head_pop2)

```

```{r}
  select(sex, Freq)

pop.nationality <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "Nationality") |> 
  filter(Group != "Missing") |> 
  mutate(nationality = factor(Group,
                      levels = c("Swiss", "Northern/Western Europe", "Southern/Eastern Europe", "Other"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(nationality, Freq)


pop.ssep <- data_general_population |> 
  filter(Variable == "SSEP") |> 
  mutate(swiss_sep_3_quintile = factor(Group,
                                     levels = c("Quintile 1", "Quintile 2","Quintile 3","Quintile 4","Quintile 5"),
                                     labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))) |> 
  mutate(Freq = proportion_genpop) |> 
  select(swiss_sep_3_quintile, Freq)


data_to_rake_bmi_pop2 <- data_bmi_pop2 |>
  select(weight_id, participant_id, age_group_bmi, sex, nationality_group_middle, swiss_sep_3_quintile, analysis_weight) |> 
  mutate(age = factor(age_group_bmi,
                      levels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17"),
                      labels = c("Infancy: <1", "Preschool age: 1–5", "School age: 6–11", "Adolescence: 12–17")),
         sex = factor(case_when(sex == "f" ~ "Female",
                                sex == "m" ~ "Male"),
                      levels = c("Female", "Male")),
         nationality = factor(nationality_group_middle,
                              levels = c("Swiss", "Northern/Western Europe", "Southern/Eastern Europe", "Other")),
         swiss_sep_3_quintile = factor(swiss_sep_3_quintile,
                                     levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))) |> 
  select(weight_id, participant_id, age, sex, nationality, swiss_sep_3_quintile, analysis_weight) |> 
  drop_na()



data_raked_bmi_pop2 <- rake(svydesign(ids = ~participant_id, data = data_to_rake_bmi_pop2, weights = ~analysis_weight),
                        sample.margins = list(~age, ~sex, ~nationality, ~swiss_sep_3_quintile),
                        population.margins = list(pop.age, pop.sex, pop.nationality, pop.ssep))

weights_bmi_pop2 <- data.frame(weight_id = data_to_rake_bmi_pop2$weight_id,
                                      genpop_weight = weights(data_raked_bmi_pop2),
                                      stabilized_genpop_weight = weights(data_raked_bmi_pop2)/mean(weights(data_raked_bmi_pop2)))

summary(weights_bmi_pop2$stabilized_genpop_weight)


# add weights back to data

data_bmi_pop2 <- data_bmi_pop2 |> 
  left_join(weights_bmi_pop2 |> select(weight_id, genpop_weight), by = "weight_id")

data_bmi_pop2 <- data_bmi_pop2 |> 
  mutate(genpop_analysis_weight = genpop_weight/number_bmi_measurements_total,
         stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight = genpop_analysis_weight*26971/sum(genpop_analysis_weight))

sum(data_bmi_pop2$genpop_weight)
sum(data_bmi_pop2$genpop_analysis_weight)
sum(data_bmi_pop2$stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

summary(data_bmi_pop2$stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

rm(data_to_rake_bmi_pop2, data_raked_bmi_pop2)

```

```{r}
                           Group == "4" ~ "Quintile 4",
                           Group == "5" ~ "Quintile 5")) |> 
  filter(!is.na(Group))


table_participant_bmi_pop2 <- table_participant_bmi_pop2 |> 
  separate(
    col = output, 
    into = c("n", "proportion"), 
    sep = " \\("
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    n = str_remove_all(n, ","),
    proportion = str_remove_all(proportion, "[%\\)]")
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    n = as.numeric(n),
    proportion = as.numeric(proportion)
  ) |> 
  mutate(proportion = as.numeric(proportion)/100)

table_participant_bmi_pop2 <- table_participant_bmi_pop2 |> 
  rename("n_SwissPedGrowth" = "n", "proportion_SwissPedGrowth" = "proportion")


standardized_difference_table_bmi_pop2_after <- data_general_population |>
  left_join(table_participant_bmi_pop2, by = "Group") |> 
  mutate(weighting = "After weighting")


standardized_difference_table_bmi_pop2_after <- standardized_difference_table_bmi_pop2_after |> 
  mutate(SPD = 2*(asin(sqrt(proportion_SwissPedGrowth)) - asin(sqrt(proportion_genpop))))

standardized_difference_table_bmi_pop2_after |> select(Group, proportion_SwissPedGrowth, proportion_genpop, SPD)
```

```{r}
get_legend2 <- function(a.gplot){
  if (!gtable::is.gtable(a.gplot))
    a.gplot <- ggplotGrob(a.gplot)
  leg <- which(sapply(a.gplot$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
  a.gplot$grobs[[leg]]
}
```

```{r}
get_legend2 <- function(a.gplot){
  if (!gtable::is.gtable(a.gplot))
    a.gplot <- ggplotGrob(a.gplot)
  leg <- which(sapply(a.gplot$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
  a.gplot$grobs[[leg]]
}

legend <- get_legend2(legend_plot)

density_plot <- plot_grid(density_height_pop1_pop2 + theme(legend.position = "None"),
                          density_weight_pop1_pop2 + theme(legend.position = "None"),
                          density_bmi_pop1_pop2 + theme(legend.position = "None"),
                          density_head_pop1_pop2 + theme(legend.position = "None"),
                          ncol=2,
                          align = "hv")

density_plot_legend <- plot_grid(density_plot,
                                 legend,
                                 ncol = 1,
                                 rel_heights = c(1, 0.2))


density_plot_legend
```

```{r}
  rename("CH-WHO 2011" = "z_height_braegger",
         "Swiss 2026" = "z_height_eiholzer",
         "Sempé 1979" = "z_height_sempe",
         "Prader 1989" = "z_height_prader")

plot_data <- plot_data |> 
  pivot_longer(names_to = "growth_reference", values_to ="z_height", cols = c("CH-WHO 2011", "Swiss 2026", "Sempé 1979", "Prader 1989"))

density_height_pop2 <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=z_height))+
  stat_function(fun=dnorm,
                n = 1000,
                linetype="solid", linewidth=0.75, aes(color="SND"))+
  stat_density(geom = "line", position = "identity", linewidth=0.75, adjust = 2, linetype = "dashed", aes(color=growth_reference, weight = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight))+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=0),
             color="black", linetype="dashed", size=0.5)+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=-0.5),
             color="black", linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.25)+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=0.5),
             color="black", linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.25)+
  scale_color_manual(breaks = c("Sempé 1979", "Prader 1989", "CH-WHO 2011", "Swiss 2026", "SND"),
                     values = c(unibeApricot(), unibeIce(), unibeRed(), unibeMint(), "black"))+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.5), xlim = c(-5,5), expand = FALSE)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(-5,-4,-3,-2,-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1,2,3,4,5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4))+
  ylab("Density")+
  xlab("Height z-score")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(size = 0.5, colour = "black", linetype="solid",),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11, colour = "black", face = "bold"),
    title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(t= 10,
                         r = 10,
                         l = 10,
                         b = 10)
  )


density_height_pop2

ggsave(filename=file.path(here("output","figures","density_height_pop2.svg")),density_height_pop2,device=svg,units="cm", height=10, width=26, bg = "white")
```

### Figure 2: Mean z-scores over age pop1 vs pop2

I use penalized cubic B-spline regression on age to check whether the fit of the growth references changes over age.
The B-splines are cubic (m=c(3)) and the penalty is set on the second derivative (m=c(3,2)).
The regression model automatically puts knots at the beginning and end, trying to reduce boundary effects.

Height

```{r}


# Girls

plot_spline_height_girls_pop1_pop2 <- ggplot(data_height_pop1 |> filter(sex == "f"), aes(x = age_years_height))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, size = 0.5, linetype = "longdash", color="black")+
  geom_smooth(method = "gam",
              formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "bs", m=c(3,2)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2,
              aes(linetype="'All children' sample", weight = analysis_weight, color = "Swiss 2026", fill = "Swiss 2026", y = z_height_eiholzer))+
  geom_smooth(method = "gam",
              formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "bs", m=c(3,2)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2,
              aes(linetype="'All children' sample", weight = analysis_weight, color = "CH-WHO 2011", fill = "CH-WHO 2011", y = z_height_braegger))+
  geom_smooth(data = data_height_pop2 |> filter(sex == "f"),
              method = "gam",
              formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "bs", m=c(3,2)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2,
              aes(linetype="'Normal growth and weighted' subsample", weight = analysis_weight, color = "Swiss 2026", fill = "Swiss 2026", y = z_height_eiholzer))+
  geom_smooth(data = data_height_pop2 |> filter(sex == "f"),
              method = "gam",
              formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "bs", m=c(3,2)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2,
              aes(linetype="'Normal growth and weighted' subsample", weight = analysis_weight, color = "CH-WHO 2011", fill = "CH-WHO 2011", y = z_height_braegger))+
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL,
                     breaks = c("Swiss 2026", "CH-WHO 2011"),
                     values = c(unibeMint(), unibeRed()))+
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL,
                     breaks = c("Swiss 2026", "CH-WHO 2011"),
                     values = c(unibeMint(), unibeRed()))+
  scale_linetype_manual(name = NULL,
                        breaks = c("'All children' sample", "'Normal growth and weighted' subsample"),
                        values = c("solid", "dashed"))+
  ylab("Mean height z-score")+
  xlab("Age (years)")+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1.5, 1.5), xlim = c(0,18), expand = FALSE)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0,3,6,9,12,15,18))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-1.5, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(size = 0.25, colour = "black", linetype="solid",),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black", face = "bold"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    title = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black")
  )
```

```{r}
title_girls <- ggdraw()+

legend_plot <- ggplot(data_height_pop1 |> filter(sex == "f"), aes(x = age_years_height, y = z_height_eiholzer))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, size = 0.5, linetype = "longdash", color="black")+
  geom_smooth(method = "gam",
              formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "bs", m=c(3,2)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2,
              aes(linetype="'All children' sample", weight = analysis_weight, color = "Swiss 2026"))+
  geom_smooth(data = data_height_pop2 |> filter(sex == "f"),
              method = "gam",
              formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "bs", m=c(3,2)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2,
              aes(linetype="'Normal growth and weighted' subsample", weight = analysis_weight, color = "CH-WHO 2011"))+
  scale_color_manual(name = "Growth reference",
                     breaks = c("CH-WHO 2011", "Swiss 2026"),
                     values = c(unibeRed(), unibeMint()))+
  scale_linetype_manual(name = "Population",
                        breaks = c("'All children' sample", "'Normal growth and weighted' subsample"),
                        values = c("solid", "dashed"))+
  ylab("Mean height z-score")+
  xlab("Age (years)")+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1.5, 1.5), xlim = c(0,18), expand = FALSE)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0,3,6,9,12,15,18))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-1.5, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5))+
  guides(linetype = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "black"))) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(size = 0.25, colour = "black", linetype="solid",),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black", face = "bold"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "vertical",
    legend.byrow = FALSE,
    legend.key.height = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black", face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    title = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black")
  )
  
legend_plot

get_legend2 <- function(a.gplot){
  if (!gtable::is.gtable(a.gplot))
    a.gplot <- ggplotGrob(a.gplot)
  leg <- which(sapply(a.gplot$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
  a.gplot$grobs[[leg]]
}

legend <- get_legend2(legend_plot)


plot_spline_titles <- plot_grid(title_girls, title_boys)
```

```{r}


title_girls <- ggdraw()+
  draw_label("Girls", size=11, fontface = "bold")

title_boys <- ggdraw()+
  draw_label("Boys", size=11, fontface = "bold")

get_legend2 <- function(a.gplot){
  if (!gtable::is.gtable(a.gplot))
    a.gplot <- ggplotGrob(a.gplot)
  leg <- which(sapply(a.gplot$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
  a.gplot$grobs[[leg]]
}

legend_height <- get_legend2(plot_spline_height_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm")))

legend_weight <- get_legend2(plot_spline_weight_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm")))

legend_head <- get_legend2(plot_spline_head_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm")))

legend_bmi <- get_legend2(plot_spline_bmi_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm")))


plot_spline_titles <- plot_grid(title_girls, title_boys)

plot_spline_height_zscore_age_pop1 <- plot_grid(plot_spline_height_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position="none"),
                                           plot_spline_height_boys_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                                           ncol=2,
                                           align = "h")

plot_spline_weight_zscore_age_pop1 <- plot_grid(plot_spline_weight_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position="none"),
                                           plot_spline_weight_boys_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                                           ncol=2,
                                           align = "h")

plot_spline_head_zscore_age_pop1 <- plot_grid(plot_spline_head_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position="none"),
                                           plot_spline_head_boys_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                                           ncol=2,
                                           align = "h")

plot_spline_bmi_zscore_age_pop1 <- plot_grid(plot_spline_bmi_girls_pop1 + theme(legend.position="none"),
                                           plot_spline_bmi_boys_pop1 + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                                           ncol=2,
                                           align = "h")

plot_spline_age_z_pop1 <- plot_grid(plot_spline_titles,
                             plot_spline_height_zscore_age_pop1,
                             legend_height,
                             plot_spline_weight_zscore_age_pop1,
                             legend_weight,
                             plot_spline_bmi_zscore_age_pop1,
                             legend_bmi,
                             plot_spline_head_zscore_age_pop1,
                             legend_head,
                             ncol = 1,
                             rel_heights = c(0.2,1,0.2,1,0.2,1,0.2,1,0.2))

plot_spline_age_z_pop1

ggsave(filename=file.path(here("output","figures","plot_spline_age_z_pop1.svg")),plot_spline_age_z_pop1,device=svg,units="cm", height=23,width=18)
```

```{r}
                     values = c(unibeApricot(), unibeIce(), unibeRed()))+

    legend.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    title = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black")
  )
```

```{r}
title_girls <- ggdraw()+
  draw_label("Girls", size=11, fontface = "bold")

title_boys <- ggdraw()+
  draw_label("Boys", size=11, fontface = "bold")

get_legend2 <- function(a.gplot){
  if (!gtable::is.gtable(a.gplot))
    a.gplot <- ggplotGrob(a.gplot)
  leg <- which(sapply(a.gplot$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
  a.gplot$grobs[[leg]]
}

legend_height <- get_legend2(plot_spline_height_girls_pop2 + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm")))
```

Function to plot centiles

```{r}

draw_centiles <- function(model, sex, parameter, base_model){
  
  z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
  z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
  z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
  z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
  z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
  z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
  z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)


  if (parameter == "height" & sex == "f") {
    
    LMS_height_girls <- data.frame(age_days_height = 0:6569) |> 
  mutate(age_days_height_trans = age_days_height^base_model$power)
    
    LMS_height_girls <- data.frame(predictAll(model, type = "response", newdata = LMS_height_girls),
                               age_days_height = 0:6569) |> 
  rename("M" = "mu", "S" = "sigma", "L" = "nu", "age_days" = "age_days_height")
    
    LMS_height_girls <- LMS_height_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


plot_centiles_height_girls_points <- LMS_height_girls |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_point(data = data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls, aes(x = age_years_height, y = height_cm), stroke = NA, color = "lightgrey")+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3), linewidth = 0.5, color = "blue")+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10), linewidth = 0.5, color = "blue")+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25), linewidth = 0.5, color = "blue")+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50), linewidth = 0.5, color = "blue")+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75), linewidth = 0.5, color = "blue")+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90), linewidth = 0.5, color = "blue")+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97), linewidth = 0.5, color = "blue")+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Height (cm)",
                     limits = c(40, 200), breaks= c(40, 100, 150, 200), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Age (years)",
                     limits = c(0, 18), breaks = c(0, 6, 12, 18), expand = c(0,0))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "black"),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0.5, l = 0.5, b = 0, unit = "cm"))


print(plot_centiles_height_girls_points)
```

### Height

#### Girls

```{r}

data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_height_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "f") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_height, age_years_height, height_cm, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_height)

data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_height/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_height, y = height_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  filter(age_years_height <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_height, y = height_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_height_girls_base <- lms(y = height_cm, x = age_days_height,
                                     data = data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_height_girls_base$power

data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_height_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_days_height_trans = age_days_height^model_height_girls_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_height_girls_base, sex = "f", parameter = "height", base_model = model_height_girls_base)

```

A transformation with 0.44 is the power transformation parameter and the BCTo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be slightly overfitted.

Take the k = 8 model.

Compare the centiles to those of Swiss 2026.

Predict LMS

```{r}
LMS_height_girls <- data.frame(age_days_height = 0:6569) |> 
  mutate(age_days_height_trans = age_days_height^model_height_girls_base$power)

LMS_height_girls <- data.frame(predictAll(gamlss_model_height_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1.4, type = "response", newdata = LMS_height_girls),
                               age_days_height = 0:6569) |> 
  rename("M" = "mu", "S" = "sigma", "L" = "nu", "age_days" = "age_days_height")

```
Plot

```{r}

z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)


interpolated_eiholzer_height <- interpolated_eiholzer_height |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  filter(age_days <= 6569)

interpolated_eiholzer_height <- interpolated_eiholzer_height |> 
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))

LMS_height_girls <- LMS_height_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


plot_centiles_height_girls <- LMS_height_girls |> 
  mutate(growth_reference = "SwissPedGrowth") |> 
  bind_rows(interpolated_eiholzer_height |> mutate(growth_reference = "Swiss 2026") |> filter(sex == "f")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
```

#### Boys

```{r}

data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_height_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_height, age_years_height, height_cm, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_height)

data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_height/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_height, y = height_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  filter(age_years_height <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_height, y = height_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_height_boys_base <- lms(y = height_cm, x = age_days_height,
                                     data = data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_height_boys_base$power

data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_days_height_trans = age_days_height^model_height_boys_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_height_boys_base, sex = "m", parameter = "height", base_model = model_height_boys_base)

```

A transformation with 0.51 is the power transformation parameter and the BCTo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be slightly overfitted.

```{r}

gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCTo <- gamlss(height_cm ~ pbm(age_days_height_trans),
                                          sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_height_trans),
                                          nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_height_trans),
                                          family = BCTo,
                                          data = data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                          weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)


gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo <- gamlss(height_cm ~ pbm(age_days_height_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_height_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_height_trans),
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1 <- gamlss(height_cm ~ pbm(age_days_height_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_height_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~1,
                                                    nu.fix = TRUE,
                                                    nu.start = 1,
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

age_groups <- c(730, 2191.5, 4383)


plot_worm_weight_boys <- wp(gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCTo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_height, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)

plot_worm_weight_boys <- wp(gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_height, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)

plot_worm_weight_boys <- wp(gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, 
   xvar = ~age_days_height, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)


fittedPlot(gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCTo,gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo, gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, x=data_height_pop2_gamlss_boys$age_days_height, line.type=c(1,2,3))

draw_centiles(gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCTo, sex = "m", parameter = "height", base_model = model_height_boys_base)
draw_centiles(gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo, sex = "m", parameter = "height", base_model = model_height_boys_base)
draw_centiles(gamlss_model_height_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, sex = "m", parameter = "height", base_model = model_height_boys_base)

```

The centiles seem fine.

I will therefore choose a model with BCCGo nu = 1.

### Weight

#### Girls

```{r}

data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_weight_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "f") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_weight, age_years_weight, weight_kg, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_weight)

data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_weight/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_weight, y = weight_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  filter(age_years_weight <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_weight, y = weight_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_weight_girls_base <- lms(y = weight_kg, x = age_days_weight,
                                     data = data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_weight_girls_base$power

data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_days_weight_trans = age_days_weight^model_weight_girls_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_weight_girls_base, sex = "f", parameter = "weight", base_model = model_weight_girls_base)

```

A transformation with 0.67 is the power transformation parameter and the BCPEo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be overfitted.

```{r}

gamlss_model_weight_girls_weighted.BCPEo <- gamlss(weight_kg ~ pbm(age_days_weight_trans),
                                          sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_weight_trans),
                                          nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_weight_trans),
                                          family = BCPEo,
                                          data = data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                          weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)


gamlss_model_weight_girls_weighted.BCCGo <- gamlss(weight_kg ~ pbm(age_days_weight_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_weight_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_weight_trans),
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

gamlss_model_weight_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1 <- gamlss(weight_kg ~ pbm(age_days_weight_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_weight_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~1,
                                                    nu.fix = TRUE,
                                                    nu.start = 1,
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_weight_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

age_groups <- c(730, 2191.5, 4383)


plot_worm_weight_girls <- wp(gamlss_model_weight_girls_weighted.BCPEo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_weight,

   show.given = FALSE)
```

#### Boys

```{r}

data_weight_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_weight_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_weight, age_years_weight, weight_kg, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_weight)

data_weight_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_weight/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_weight_pop2_gamlss_boys |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_weight, y = weight_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_weight_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  filter(age_years_weight <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_weight, y = weight_kg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_weight_boys_base <- lms(y = weight_kg, x = age_days_weight,
                                     data = data_weight_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_weight_boys_base$power

data_weight_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_weight_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_days_weight_trans = age_days_weight^model_weight_boys_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_weight_boys_base, sex = "m", parameter = "weight", base_model = model_weight_boys_base)

```

A transformation with 0.27 is the power transformation parameter and the BCPEo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be slightly overfitted.

```{r}

gamlss_model_weight_boys_weighted.BCPEo <- gamlss(weight_kg ~ pbm(age_days_weight_trans),
                                          sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_weight_trans),
                                          nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_weight_trans),
```

### Head circumference

#### Girls

```{r}

data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_head_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "f") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_circumference, age_years_circumference, head_cm, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_circumference)

data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_circumference/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_circumference, y = head_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  filter(age_years_circumference <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_circumference, y = head_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_head_girls_base <- lms(y = head_cm, x = age_days_circumference,
                                     data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_head_girls_base$power

data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_days_circumference_trans = age_days_circumference^model_head_girls_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_head_girls_base, sex = "f", parameter = "head", base_model = model_head_girls_base)

```

A transformation with 0.59 is the power transformation parameter and the BCTo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be slightly overfitted.

```{r}

gamlss_model_head_girls_weighted.BCTo <- gamlss(head_cm ~ pbm(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                          sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                          nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                          family = BCTo,
                                          data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                          weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)


gamlss_model_head_girls_weighted.BCCGo <- gamlss(head_cm ~ pbm(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

gamlss_model_head_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1 <- gamlss(head_cm ~ pbm(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~1,
                                                    nu.fix = TRUE,
                                                    nu.start = 1,
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

age_groups <- c(730, 2191.5, 4383)


plot_worm_weight_girls <- wp(gamlss_model_head_girls_weighted.BCTo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_circumference, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)

plot_worm_weight_girls <- wp(gamlss_model_head_girls_weighted.BCCGo,
```

The sigma parameter seems to be overfitted when using the default pb function.


Use GAIC

```{r}


max_k <- log(sum(data_head_pop2_gamlss_girls$stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight))

max_k

```




The centiles of the ML model seem slightly overfitted.
The centiles of all GAIC models seem very similar regardless of k = 2 or k = log n.

Take the k = 4 model.

Compare the centiles to those of Swiss 2026.

Predict LMS

```{r}
LMS_head_girls <- data.frame(age_days_circumference = 0:6569) |> 
  mutate(age_days_circumference_trans = age_days_circumference^model_head_girls_base$power)

LMS_head_girls <- data.frame(predictAll(gamlss_model_head_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1.2, type = "response", newdata = LMS_head_girls),
                               age_days_circumference = 0:6569) |> 
  rename("M" = "mu", "S" = "sigma", "L" = "nu", "age_days" = "age_days_circumference")

```
Plot

```{r}

z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)


interpolated_braegger_head_circumference <- interpolated_braegger_head_circumference |>
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  filter(age_days <= 6569)

interpolated_braegger_head_circumference <- interpolated_braegger_head_circumference |>
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))

LMS_head_girls <- LMS_head_girls |>
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


plot_centiles_head_girls <- LMS_head_girls |>
  mutate(growth_reference = "SwissPedGrowth") |>
  bind_rows(interpolated_braegger_head_circumference |> mutate(growth_reference = "CH-WHO 2011") |> filter(sex == "f")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Head circumference (cm)",
                     limits = c(30, 60), breaks= c(30, 40, 50, 60), expand = c(0,0),
                     minor_breaks = c(seq(30,60,by =1)))+
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Age (years)",
                     limits = c(0, 18), breaks = c(0, 6, 12, 18), expand = c(0,0),
                     minor_breaks = c(seq(0,18,by =1)))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("CH-WHO 2011" = unibeRed(), "SwissPedGrowth" = "black"))+
  scale_linetype_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("CH-WHO 2011" = "solid", "SwissPedGrowth" = "dashed"))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", color = "black"),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 0.25, r = 0.25, l = 0.25, b = 0, unit = "cm"))

  scale_linetype_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("CH-WHO 2011" = "solid", "SwissPedGrowth" = "dashed"))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", color = "black"),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 0.25, r = 0.25, l = 0.25, b = 0, unit = "cm"))


plot_centiles_head_girls_2yr


png(here("output", "figures", "wormplot_head_girls.png"), width = 9, height = 12, unit = "cm", res = 600)
wp(gamlss_model_head_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1.2,
   xvar = ~age_days_circumference,
   xcut.points = age_groups,
   ylim.worm = 1,
   line = TRUE,
   col = unibeRed(),
   cex = 0.5,
   lwd = 2.5,
   show.given = FALSE)
dev.off()

```


#### Boys

```{r}

data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_head_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_circumference, age_years_circumference, head_cm, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_circumference)

data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_circumference/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_circumference, y = head_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  filter(age_years_circumference <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_circumference, y = head_cm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_head_boys_base <- lms(y = head_cm, x = age_days_circumference,
                                     data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_head_boys_base$power

data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_days_circumference_trans = age_days_circumference^model_head_boys_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_head_boys_base, sex = "m", parameter = "head", base_model = model_head_boys_base)

```

A transformation with 0.51 is the power transformation parameter and the BCTo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be slightly overfitted.

```{r}

gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCTo <- gamlss(head_cm ~ pbm(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                          sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                          nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                          family = BCTo,
                                          data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                          weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)


gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo <- gamlss(head_cm ~ pbm(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1 <- gamlss(head_cm ~ pbm(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_circumference_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~1,
                                                    nu.fix = TRUE,
                                                    nu.start = 1,
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

age_groups <- c(730, 2191.5, 4383)


plot_worm_weight_boys <- wp(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCTo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_circumference, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)

plot_worm_weight_boys <- wp(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_circumference, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)

plot_worm_weight_boys <- wp(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, 
   xvar = ~age_days_circumference, 
   xcut.points = age_groups,

   show.given = FALSE)


fittedPlot(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCTo,gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo, gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, x=data_head_pop2_gamlss_boys$age_days_circumference, line.type=c(1,2,3))

draw_centiles(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCTo, sex = "m", parameter = "head", base_model = model_head_boys_base)
draw_centiles(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo, sex = "m", parameter = "head", base_model = model_head_boys_base)
draw_centiles(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, sex = "m", parameter = "head", base_model = model_head_boys_base)
```

Predict LMS

```{r}

LMS_head_boys <- data.frame(age_days_circumference = 0:6569) |> 
  mutate(age_days_circumference_trans = age_days_circumference^model_head_boys_base$power)

LMS_head_boys <- data.frame(predictAll(gamlss_model_head_boys_weighted.BCCGo.nu1.4, type = "response", newdata = LMS_head_boys),
                               age_days_circumference = 0:6569) |> 
  rename("M" = "mu", "S" = "sigma", "L" = "nu", "age_days" = "age_days_circumference")

```
Plot

```{r}

z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)


interpolated_braegger_head_circumference <- interpolated_braegger_head_circumference |>
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  filter(age_days <= 6569)

interpolated_braegger_head_circumference <- interpolated_braegger_head_circumference |>
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))

LMS_head_boys <- LMS_head_boys |>
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))

  mutate(growth_reference = "SwissPedGrowth") |>
  bind_rows(interpolated_braegger_head_circumference |> mutate(growth_reference = "CH-WHO 2011") |> filter(sex == "m")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+

  scale_y_continuous(name = "Head circumference (cm)",
                     limits = c(30, 65), breaks= c(30, 40, 50, 60), expand = c(0,0),
```
