### BMI

#### Girls

```{r}

data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_bmi_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "f") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_bmi, age_years_bmi, bmi, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_bmi)

data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_bmi/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_bmi, y = bmi)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  filter(age_years_bmi <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_bmi, y = bmi)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_bmi_girls_base <- lms(y = bmi, x = age_days_bmi,
                                     data = data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_bmi_girls_base$power

data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls <- data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls |> 
  mutate(age_days_bmi_trans = age_days_bmi^model_bmi_girls_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_bmi_girls_base, sex = "f", parameter = "bmi", base_model = model_bmi_girls_base)

```

A transformation with 0.59 is the power transformation parameter and the BCPEo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be slightly overfitted.

```{r}

gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCPEo <- gamlss(bmi ~ pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                          sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                          nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                          family = BCPEo,
                                          data = data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                          weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)


gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo <- gamlss(bmi ~ pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1 <- gamlss(bmi ~ pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                                    sigma.formula = ~pb(age_days_bmi_trans),
                                                    nu.formula = ~1,
                                                    nu.fix = TRUE,
                                                    nu.start = 1,
                                                    family = BCCGo,
                                                    data = data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls,
                                                    weights = stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight)

age_groups <- c(730, 2191.5, 4383)


plot_worm_weight_girls <- wp(gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCPEo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_bmi, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)

plot_worm_weight_girls <- wp(gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo, 
   xvar = ~age_days_bmi, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)

plot_worm_weight_girls <- wp(gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, 
   xvar = ~age_days_bmi, 
   xcut.points = age_groups, 
   ylim.worm = 1,
   show.given = FALSE)


fittedPlot(gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCPEo,gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo, gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, x=data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_girls$age_days_bmi, line.type=c(1,2,3))

draw_centiles(gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCPEo, sex = "f", parameter = "bmi", base_model = model_bmi_girls_base)
draw_centiles(gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo, sex = "f", parameter = "bmi", base_model = model_bmi_girls_base)
draw_centiles(gamlss_model_bmi_girls_weighted.BCCGo.nu1, sex = "f", parameter = "bmi", base_model = model_bmi_girls_base)

```

The sigma parameter seems to be overfitted when using the default pb function.

#### Boys

```{r}

data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_bmi_pop2 |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  select(sex, age_days_bmi, age_years_bmi, bmi, stabilized_genpop_analysis_weight) |> 
  arrange(age_days_bmi)

data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_group = factor(floor(age_days_bmi/365.25))) |> 
  select(age_group) |> 
  tbl_summary()


data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_boys |> ggplot(aes(x = age_years_bmi, y = bmi)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  filter(age_years_bmi <=2) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years_bmi, y = bmi)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, stroke = NA)


```

Use approach described in the book Flexible Regression and Smoothing Using GAMLSS in R as method 3 in the chapter 13 Centile estimation.
- step 1: find a suitable transformation for the age to get a better fit if there is an early or late fast growth. In our case, we expect this in infancy between 0 and 1 year.
- step 2: Use the found age transformation and estimate the degrees of freedom hyperparameters (mu, sigma, nu, tau).

These two steps are implemented in the lms() function.


```{r}
model_bmi_boys_base <- lms(y = bmi, x = age_days_bmi,
                                     data = data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_boys,
                                     trans.x = TRUE)

model_bmi_boys_base$power

data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_boys <- data_bmi_pop2_gamlss_boys |> 
  mutate(age_days_bmi_trans = age_days_bmi^model_bmi_boys_base$power)

draw_centiles(model_bmi_boys_base, sex = "f", parameter = "bmi", base_model = model_bmi_boys_base)

```

A transformation with 0.29 is the power transformation parameter and the BCPEo family seems to yield the best fitting centiles.
However, they seem to be slightly overfitted.


The centiles of the ML model seem slightly overfitted.
The centiles of all GAIC models seem very similar regardless of k = 2 or k = log n.

Take the k = 6 model.

Compare the centiles to those of Eiholzer.

Predict LMS

```{r}
LMS_bmi_boys <- data.frame(age_days_bmi = 0:6569) |> 
  mutate(age_days_bmi_trans = age_days_bmi^model_bmi_boys_base$power)

LMS_bmi_boys <- data.frame(predictAll(gamlss_model_bmi_boys_weighted.BCCGo.3, type = "response", newdata = LMS_bmi_boys),
                               age_days_bmi = 0:6569) |> 
  rename("M" = "mu", "S" = "sigma", "L" = "nu", "age_days" = "age_days_bmi")

```

```{r}

z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)


interpolated_eiholzer_bmi <- interpolated_eiholzer_bmi |>
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>
  filter(age_days <= 6569)

interpolated_eiholzer_bmi <- interpolated_eiholzer_bmi |>
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))

LMS_bmi_boys <- LMS_bmi_boys |>
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25) |>

  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +

  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = growth_reference, linetype = growth_reference), linewidth = 0.5)+
```
